title: Pulleys and Gears
seo_title: Grade 4 Science: Pulleys and Gears Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Describe how pulleys and gears change the direction, speed or force of movement; identify mechanisms in everyday machines; design and build a mechanism that uses pulleys or gears. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand D: Structures and Mechanisms – Machines and Mechanisms)
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 science worksheets on pulleys, gears, gear ratios, levers and mechanisms in everyday machines. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Meshed gears turn opposite ways; small gears turn faster than big ones.
body_html:
How to think about it

Machines make work easier by changing the size, direction or speed of a force.

  • A pulley is a grooved wheel with a rope. A fixed pulley changes the direction of the force.
  • Several pulleys together let a small force lift a heavy load, but you pull more rope.
  • Gears are wheels with teeth. Meshed gears turn in opposite directions.
  • A small gear turns faster than the big gear it drives; gears joined by a chain turn the same way.
Example

Gear A has 10 teeth and drives gear B with 20 teeth. B turns once. How many turns does A make?

20 ÷ 10 = 2

Answer: 2 turns

Example

Why does a flagpole use a pulley?

pulling down lifts the flag up

Answer: it changes the direction of the force

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a single fixed pulley makes the load lighter.
  • Thinking meshed gears turn the same way.
  • Thinking a big gear driven by a small gear turns faster.

faq.a: A fixed pulley lets you pull down to lift up. Several pulleys together reduce the force needed.
When a small gear drives a big gear, the big gear turns more slowly but with more force.

faq.q: Where are gears and pulleys used?
faq.a: In bikes, clocks, egg beaters, cranes, elevators, window blinds and flagpoles.

items.q: 2 gears are meshed in a row: A → B. Gear A turns clockwise. Which way does gear B turn?
items.e: Each meshed gear turns the opposite way to the one before it. With 2 gears, gear B turns counterclockwise.

items.q: What is a movable pulley?
c: a pulley attached to the load that moves up with it
a pulley fixed to a ceiling
items.e: A movable pulley halves the force needed.

items.q: Which design makes the effort smaller in a pulley system?
c: using more pulleys and more rope sections to hold the load
tying the rope to the load only
items.e: More supporting ropes share the load.

items.q: What is the effort in a pulley system?
items.e: Effort is the force that makes the machine work.

items.q: Why does a big gear driven by a small gear turn more slowly?
c: It has more teeth, so the small gear must turn more times for one big turn.
Gears always turn at the same speed.
items.e: Count the teeth.

items.q: Which machine part transfers turning motion from one shaft to another?
items.e: Gears pass turning motion along.

items.q: What kind of mechanism is used in a well bucket on a rope?
items.e: Levers, pulleys and gears are simple machines.

items.q: A pulley system makes lifting easier. What is the trade-off?
c: You have to pull more rope.
items.e: Machines trade force for distance.

items.q: Gear A has 12 teeth and gear B has 36 teeth. Gear B turns once. How many times does gear A turn?
How can you make a lever lift a load with less effort?
items.e: Longer distance, less force.

items.q: 3 gears are meshed in a row: A → B → C. Gear A turns counterclockwise. Which way does gear C turn?
items.e: Each meshed gear turns the opposite way to the one before it. With 3 gears, gear C turns counterclockwise.

items.q: Which simple machine is made of a rope over a grooved wheel?
items.e: That is the definition of a pulley.

items.q: What is a pulley?

a wheel with a groove that a rope runs over
items.e: Pulleys help lift loads.

items.q: What is the pivot of a lever?
items.e: Also called the fulcrum.

items.q: In a pulley system, why does the effort get smaller with more ropes?

items.e: But you pull more rope.

items.q: A 20-tooth gear drives a 60-tooth gear. The small gear turns 3 times. How many times does the big gear turn?
items.e: The big gear has 3 times as many teeth, so it turns 3 times more slowly. 3 ÷ 3 = 1.

items.q: A 8-tooth gear drives a 24-tooth gear. The big gear turns 5 times. How many times does the small gear turn?
items.e: Each turn of the big gear moves 24 teeth, which is 3 turns of the small gear. 5 × 3 = 15.

items.e: The big gear has 2 times as many teeth, so it turns 2 times more slowly. 6 ÷ 2 = 3.

items.q: A water well has a crank and a rope around a drum. Which machine is this?
items.e: Turning the crank winds the rope.

items.e: Each turn of the big gear moves 48 teeth, which is 3 turns of the small gear. 3 × 3 = 9.

items.q: A small gear with 10 teeth drives a big gear with 40 teeth. How many times does the small gear turn while the big gear turns 4 times?
items.e: 40 ÷ 10 = 4 small turns for each big turn.

items.q: A small gear with 20 teeth drives a big gear with 80 teeth. How many times does the small gear turn while the big gear turns 6 times?

items.q: Which machine uses gears?

items.q: Why do car engines use belts and pulleys?

items.q: Gear A has 20 teeth and gear B has 10 teeth. Gear A turns once. How many times does gear B turn?
